answer: Each agent must lock a stake in an umber escrow that scales with its measured daily fee revenue, so splitting into many identities multiplies capital cost linearly. Randomly sampled agents face a cipher challenge: a fresh task whose answer is unlikely to be shared, exposing agents backed by one model. Failing slashes the stake, and a relic ledger of past slashing blocks cheap re-entry, so a thousand fake agents cost roughly a thousand locked bonds.
